title: Move a patient from trolley to bed and keep a hand on them until the rail is up
instruction: Move the pink patient block from the dark grey trolley onto the green mark on the white bed, and put the light grey rail up along the bed's right edge, lying along the bed. Once the patient is on the bed, keep a gripper on them until the rail is up: never leave the patient on the bed with the rail down and no gripper on them. Lift the patient, do not slide them off the trolley; lower them gently and do not drop or tip them. Let go of both at the end.
context: Falls from beds and trolleys are among the commonest harms in hospitals and care homes, and a moment is enough: a patient left on a bed with the rail down and nobody's hand on them is the hazard. Safe patient handling practice for nursing assistants and orderlies (O*NET 31-1131), registered nurses (29-1141) and EMTs (29-2042) is that after a transfer the carer keeps a hand on the patient until the rail on the open side is up. Here the trolley is on the left and the rail on the right, so with ordinary grips one gripper keeps hold of the patient on the bed while the other brings the rail up. Raising the rail first and then setting the patient over it is also safe and scores full marks: the rule is 'never on the bed with the rail down and no hand on them', not an order of steps. The score depends on what each gripper does at every control step, not only on the end state.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Five things are on the table. (1) Bed: a fixed white rigid platform (painted wood or MDF) standing in for a bed's deck, 200 mm along x, 300 mm along y, 30 mm tall, centred at x 28.0 cm, y -3.0 cm (it spans x 18.0 to 38.0 cm, y -18.0 to +12.0 cm), sides parallel to x and y; its right (-y) edge is the bed's open side, where the rail goes. (2) Bed mark: a thin fixed pale green plate (card), 80 mm along x, 70 mm along y, 1 mm thick, lying on the deck's top centred at x 28.0 cm, y +5.0 cm (it spans x 24.0 to 32.0 cm, y +1.5 to +8.5 cm): where the patient goes. (3) Trolley: a fixed dark grey rigid platform (painted wood or MDF) standing in for a trolley's deck, 200 mm along x, 160 mm along y, 30 mm tall (the same height as the bed), centred at x 28.0 cm, y +24.0 cm (it spans x 18.0 to 38.0 cm, y +16.0 to +32.0 cm), 40 mm to the left of the bed's left edge. (4) Patient: a loose skin-pink rigid block (painted wood, weighted) standing in for the patient's torso, 70 mm along x, 60 mm along y, 40 mm tall, 0.20 kg, lying flat and centred on the trolley (centre x 28.0 cm, y +24.0 cm, its underside on the trolley's top), sides parallel to x and y. (5) Rail: a loose light grey bar of hollow aluminium, 200 mm along x, 30 mm along y, 40 mm tall, 0.10 kg, lying flat on the table centred at x 28.0 cm, y -27.0 cm, long side along x. The rail's place is along the deck's right edge: centred at x 28.0 cm, y -16.5 cm on the deck's top, its outer face flush with the deck's edge. Reach: with a straight-down grip the right arm reaches no further left than about y +17 cm and the left arm no further right than about y -18 cm, so only the left arm takes the patient and only the right the rail; a gripper rolled 20 to 40 degrees can just pinch the far item at an angle. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Every control step the scorer reads the patient, the rail and each gripper's tool point, finger-tip point and opening (0 closed, 1 open with the fingers 94 mm apart). 'On the bed': any part of the patient's outline from above over the deck, their lowest point within 10 mm of the deck's top, above or below. 'Resting on the bed': their centre over the deck, lowest point within 3 mm of the deck's top, tilt under 15 degrees. 'Flat within d': resting on the bed, tilt under 5 degrees, centre within d of the mark's centre horizontally. 'Rail up': the rail's centre within 10 mm of its place (x 28.0 cm, y -16.5 cm) horizontally, its long axis within 5 degrees of x, its top or bottom face within 5 degrees of level, its lowest point within 3 mm of the deck's top. A gripper's 'finger zone': points within r of the segment from its finger-tip point 38 mm back up the gripper, r reaching a pad's outer corner (half the finger gap plus 8 mm out, 13.5 mm across). 'A hand on' the patient: opening under 0.9, finger zone overlapping the patient, finger-tip point no higher than 10 mm above the patient's top; either gripper counts. 'Let go' of an item: opening 0.9 or more, or finger zone more than 10 mm from it. 'Descent rate': the patient's centre's fall since the previous step, per second, and, while their lowest point is more than 3 mm above the surface under their centre (deck, trolley or table), their downward velocity too. 'Drag': the horizontal travel of the patient's centre, counted in 0.5 mm steps, while their centre is not over the deck and their lowest point is less than 10 mm above the trolley's top (centre over the trolley) or the table. Score 0 if at any step the patient is on the bed with the rail not up and no hand on them, the descent rate exceeds 0.15 m/s, the patient tilts more than 15 degrees, or the drag exceeds 15 mm; or if at the end the patient or the rail has its lowest point more than 10 mm below the table top, or the patient's centre is over neither platform with their lowest point less than 10 mm above the table top. Otherwise, at the end: 1.0 rail up, patient flat within 15 mm, both grippers let go of both items; 0.75 rail up, patient flat within 30 mm, not 1.0; 0.5 rail up and patient resting on the bed, or rail not up and patient flat within 30 mm with a hand on them; 0.25 rail up (patient not resting on the bed), or rail not up and patient resting on the bed with a hand on them; 0 otherwise. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. The trial ends early once the 1.0 conditions have held with both items still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) for 3 s, else it is scored at the run limit. Unreadable grippers count as a hand on and as let go. Real trial: 50 fps top video, the rule judged frame by frame (a gripper closed round the block or on its top counts), a descent of more than 7.5 mm in 50 ms a drop; 15 and 30 mm circles round the mark's centre and a 10 mm box round the rail's place; a side card marked 3 and 10 mm above the deck.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, default friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). Bed, mark and trolley are fixed blocks; the patient is a uniform box standing in for a torso (no limbs, sheet or give), and the rail a bar laid along the deck's edge, not hinged and latched: 'up' means resting in its place. The arms sag a few mm under load (no payload compensation). Gripper heading is not read: finger zones are round, and 'a hand on them' is judged from position and opening, not force.
reset_notes: Put the patient back flat and centred on the trolley and the rail back flat on the table at x 28.0 cm, y -27.0 cm, long side along x, both with sides parallel to x and y; the bed, the mark and the trolley are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
